questions.question: An advanced provider's skill set includes starting a line in a vein to give certain emergency medications. What is that skill called?
Which term is defined as: "An established process to determine the qualifications necessary to be allowed to practice a particular profession, or to function as an organization"?
questions.explanation: The deck defines credentialing as the established process to determine the qualifications necessary to practice or function as an organization.

questions.question: YOU are the Provider (48-year-old woman, back pain): Does this patient need any treatment at the scene that can be provided by an EMT?
choices: Yes; the EMT should obtain online medical control orders before any assessment or transport decision is made
No treatment is needed, so the call can be closed as nonemergent once her vital signs are recorded

No immediate EMT treatment exists for this patient; treat the situation as an emergency until a thorough assessment proves otherwise, reassess vital signs, provide comfort measures, and transport her in the safest, most comfortable way
Yes; the EMT should begin the system's CQI review process at the scene before moving the patient
questions.explanation: There is no immediate treatment an EMT can provide for this patient, so the call is treated as an emergency until a qualified assessment distinguishes emergent from nonemergent, with reassessment, comfort measures, and safe, comfortable transport.

questions.question: What does the term 'community paramedicine' mean?
choices: Efforts to limit the effects of an injury or illness that cannot be completely prevented
A call center staffed by trained personnel who manage requests for police, fire, and ambulance services

A health care model in which experienced paramedics receive advanced training to provide additional prehospital services, such as health evaluations, monitoring of chronic illnesses, and patient advocacy
An approach to medicine in which decisions are based on well-conducted research and the strength of the scientific evidence
questions.explanation: Community paramedicine uses experienced, additionally trained paramedics to deliver services like health evaluations and chronic illness monitoring in the prehospital environment.

questions.question: What is a primary service area?
choices: The designated area in which an EMS agency is responsible for providing prehospital emergency care and transportation to the hospital
A competent authority, usually the state, allowing a person to perform a regulated act
An established process to determine the qualifications necessary to practice a profession
Delivering health care within the community rather than at a physician's office or hospital
questions.explanation: A primary service area is the designated area where the agency owes prehospital care and transport.

questions.question: King County's continuing education program was reaccredited through CAPCE, and its Training and Education Section distributed ten new online CE courses for EMTs, paramedics, and telecommunicators. The county credits this ongoing training for letting its paramedics use an extensive array of medications and procedures. What does this show about continuing education?
choices: It replaces initial EMT training for new hires
It is only a paperwork requirement for keeping a certification
It is a disciplinary tool run by the state office of EMS
It maintains, updates, and expands provider knowledge, and is part of why providers are trusted with a wider scope of practice
questions.explanation: Continuing education is not paperwork; in King County it is part of why providers are trusted with a wider scope of practice.

questions.question: Two metro Phoenix dispatch centers adopted a telephone CPR (T-CPR) bundle of protocols, training, data, and feedback, studied across 2,334 cardiac arrests. What was the result?
choices: T-CPR delivery fell and survival stayed the same
T-CPR delivery rose from 43.5% to 52.8%, time to first compression fell, and survival rose from 9.1% to 12.0%
Survival fell because callers were kept on the phone too long
The bundle only changed documentation, not patient outcomes
questions.explanation: The deck's Phoenix case is strong evidence that dispatcher pre-arrival instructions save lives: T-CPR delivery and survival both rose after the bundle was adopted.
Pharmacologic interventions and advanced treatment skills are functions of the paramedic.
questions.question: A crew requests the provider who can give pharmacologic interventions and perform other advanced assessment and treatment skills at the scene. Which provider level should respond?

questions.explanation: Proactive home-based community care for frequent 911 users is a flagship mobile integrated health care model.
questions.question: In Fort Worth, Texas, MedStar's program for frequent 911 callers sent a mobile healthcare paramedic to each patient's home for a medication and needs review, and ambulance trips to the ED dropped 47.6% among enrolled patients. This program is an example of:
A caller dials 911 and reaches a staffed center that takes the report and sends police, fire, and ambulance units as needed. What is this center called?
questions.explanation: That center manages requests for police, fire, and ambulance services; it is the public safety access point.
The program was evaluated against preset standards and formally recognized for meeting them, which the source identifies as certification.
questions.question: An EMT training program is reviewed by an outside board and is formally recognized for meeting all required education standards. What is this recognition called?

choices: Naloxone was restricted to paramedics only
EMTs were barred from giving naloxone
Naloxone was added to the EMR and EMT levels
Police departments were required to stop carrying naloxone
questions.explanation: A 2017 national change notice added naloxone to the EMR and EMT levels of the Scope of Practice Model.
questions.question: In 2010, Quincy, Massachusetts police became the first police department to carry intranasal naloxone, because officers were often the first on scene at opioid overdoses. What national scope change followed in 2017?
questions.topic: National EMS Scope of Practice Model

questions.question: In 2010, Quincy, Massachusetts police became the first department in the state's naloxone program: every officer was trained and carried nasal naloxone, and officers usually reach overdoses before the ambulance. From 2010 to 2013, Quincy police administered naloxone 201 times. Why does this case illustrate the emergency medical responder role?
choices: Police officers replaced EMTs as the primary responders to overdoses
Naloxone can only be given by police officers in Massachusetts
The ambulance always arrives before police at overdose calls
Police, often first to arrive, delivered a life-saving intervention before EMS — the EMR role
questions.explanation: The Quincy case connects because police, often first to arrive, delivered a life-saving EMR intervention with naloxone.
Written protocols are off-line medical control, and the DC crews did not follow them.
questions.question: In 2006, Washington DC crews found an assaulted man on a sidewalk, assumed he was drunk, recorded no vital signs, and took him to a more distant hospital instead of the closest facility their protocol required; he died of a head injury. The failure to follow the agency's written protocols on assessment, documentation, and destination is best described as a failure of:

choices: National EMS Scope of Practice Model
questions.explanation: The model is the national reference for dividing skills among EMR, EMT, AEMT, and paramedic.
questions.question: Two agencies disagree about which provider level should perform a certain airway skill, so they check the national model that sorts skills by level. What document should they check?
questions.topic: National EMS Scope of Practice Model

questions.question: Which term is defined as: "The designated area in which the EMS agency is responsible for the provision of prehospital emergency care and transportation to the hospital"?
questions.explanation: The deck defines the primary service area as the designated area where the agency is responsible for prehospital care and transport.
The campaign's goal is preventing harm across the whole population, which best fits public health.
questions.question: A city passes a seat-belt campaign aimed at every driver in the community after reviewing crash data for the whole region. Which branch of medicine does this best fit?

questions.explanation: Basic life support, AED use, and medication assistance are core EMT functions.
questions.question: A provider gives basic life support, applies an AED to an unresponsive patient, and helps the patient take a prescribed medication. What level of provider is this?

questions.explanation: Advanced life-saving procedures define advanced life support care.
questions.question: Instead of only oxygen and basic support, the crew performs advanced life-saving interventions normally associated with higher-level providers. Which type of care are they providing?

Seattle's Medic One program began after cardiologist Dr. Leonard Cobb set the training standard for firefighters in 1969, authorized advanced skills, and reviewed care from the first patient onward; the first paramedic class answered its first call in 1970. Why is this case tied to the medical director topic?
choices: It shows a physician setting training standards, authorizing skills, and reviewing care — the origin of the medical director role
It shows the first use of an AED by bystanders
It shows a HIPAA enforcement action against a hospital
It shows why IV fluids should be delayed in trauma
questions.explanation: Cobb's role — setting training standards, authorizing advanced skills, and reviewing care — is the origin of the medical director role in EMS.
Procedures beyond basic life support are advanced life support.
questions.question: A patient's care goes beyond basic measures when the crew begins advanced airway and cardiac treatment procedures in the field. What level of care is this called?

questions.explanation: Giving out helmets and smoke alarms targets hazards early so injuries and fires are kept from occurring at all.
questions.question: A city gives away bicycle helmets and smoke alarms at a health fair and teaches families how to use them. What type of prevention is this?

Which term is defined as: "A system that assists dispatchers in selecting appropriate units to respond to a particular call for assistance and provides callers with vital instructions until the arrival of EMS crews"?
questions.explanation: The deck defines emergency medical dispatch as the system that helps dispatchers select appropriate units and provides callers vital instructions until EMS crews arrive.

choices: Her agency must cover her shifts until she finishes
She receives an automatic six-month grace period
She must stop providing EMT services as of the certification expiration date
Only her agency is penalized, not the EMT
questions.explanation: Indiana puts the burden of demonstrating compliance on the individual EMT, who must stop providing EMT services if the requirements are unmet at expiration.
questions.question: An Indiana EMT's certification is nearing its two-year expiration and she has not completed the required 40 hours of continuing education. Under the state's instructions, what happens if she does not meet the requirement?

questions.explanation: Prehospital care standards and the people who provide that care are typically regulated by the state office of EMS.
questions.question: A new EMT asks who sets and enforces the standards for prehospital care and the providers who deliver it in her state. Who is it?

Which term is defined as: a device that detects treatable life-threatening cardiac dysrhythmias (ventricular fibrillation and ventricular tachycardia) and delivers the appropriate electrical shock to the patient?
questions.explanation: An automated external defibrillator detects shockable rhythms such as VF and ventricular tachycardia and delivers a shock.

questions.question: Assessment in Action: Which of the phases of being an emergency health care provider is continuous?
questions.explanation: Book's printed key: Continuing medical education.
Pay, career progression, and EMT well-being are the human resources department's job, not the medical director's.
questions.question: An EMT asks who handles her pay raise, her promotion path, and the agency wellness program. Which department is that?
After the Tyre Nichols response in Memphis in 2023, Tennessee's EMS Board suspended two responders' licenses at an emergency meeting within days of the incident. What does this show about licensure?
choices: Licenses can only be suspended after a criminal conviction
A state board can suspend a license quickly, then hold a full hearing that can end in revocation
License discipline is handled by the provider's own agency, not the state
Suspension is the most severe action a board can take
questions.explanation: The deck's connection: a state board can suspend a license within days, then hold a full hearing that can end in revocation.
The review determines whether that person is qualified to function in that organization, which is credentialing.
questions.question: A medical director's office reviews an EMT's training file and test results before approving him for a specific role in that system. What is this review called?

questions.explanation: The medical director is checking care on an individual call, which is quality control rather than a system-wide review.
questions.question: The medical director personally reviews one EMT's patient care report from last night's call to check that the required care standard was met. What is this single-call oversight called?

choices: Accidental Death and Disability: The Neglected Disease of Modern Society
The National Scope of Practice Model
questions.explanation: EMS as we know it today is traced to that 1966 white paper's publication.
questions.question: A history question says modern EMS began with a 1966 report calling accidental death a neglected disease. What is that report?
questions.topic: Accidental Death and Disability: The Neglected Disease of Modern Society

questions.explanation: The medical director is the physician who authorizes EMTs to provide medical care in the field.
questions.question: Before an EMT crew can follow new treatment protocols, a physician reviews and signs off on them for the service. Which role is that physician filling?
What does the term "primary prevention" mean?
choices: Efforts to prevent an injury or illness from ever occurring
Oversight by the medical director to ensure care standards are met on each call
A NHTSA document outlining the skills performed by various EMS providers
Legislation protecting people with disabilities against discrimination
questions.explanation: Primary prevention means stopping an injury or illness before it ever occurs.
State EMS offices regulate practice and grant the legal authority to provide care, and that official permission is licensure.
questions.question: The state office of EMS, which regulates prehospital care standards in the state, issues an EMT his official permission to practice. What is that permission called?

After Michigan partly repealed its universal motorcycle helmet law in 2012, helmet use among injured riders dropped and head injuries among hospitalized riders rose from 43.4% to 49.6%. Why is helmet use classified as secondary prevention?
choices: Helmets prevent most motorcycle crashes from happening
Helmets eliminate the need for EMS after a crash
Helmets do not prevent crashes; they limit the severity of the injury when a crash occurs
Helmets are a form of primary prevention because they stop injuries entirely
questions.explanation: The Michigan case connects because helmets don't prevent crashes — they limit injury severity, which is secondary prevention.
Assisting patients with certain prescribed medications is part of the EMT role.
questions.question: A patient with chest discomfort is assisted with his own prescribed medication by the basic-level field provider caring for him. What is that provider called?

On April 9, 2014, a software counter at a 911 routing center in Englewood, Colorado, hit its limit and stopped routing new 911 calls. In all, 81 PSAPs in 7 states were affected and more than 6,600 calls never got through. What should EMTs expect after a 911 outage like this?
choices: Delayed calls and sicker patients, so crews should know their agency's backup plan and alternate numbers
No effect, because PSAPs never depend on outside routing networks
Fewer calls, because blocked callers do not call back
Immediate transfer of all calls to a neighboring state's PSAPs
questions.explanation: The 2014 outage case teaches EMTs to know the backup plan for a 911 outage and to expect delayed calls and sicker patients afterward.
It acts before any crash occurs, so the injury never happens in the first place.
questions.question: A community awareness program visits local high schools to emphasize the dangers of drinking and driving, hoping no crash ever happens. What type of prevention is this?

When the EMS Compact was activated for COVID-19 in March 2020, EMS personnel licensed in a member state received a "privilege to practice" in other member states. How does the Compact treat licensure?
choices: It replaces state licenses with one national license
It lets any EMT work in any state without restriction
Licenses stay state-based; the Compact is how member states recognize each other's licenses
It is run by the NREMT as a certification program
questions.explanation: The deck states that licenses stay state-based and the Compact is how member states recognize each other's licenses.

questions.question: Which term is defined as: 'A health care model in which experienced paramedics receive advanced training to equip them to provide additional services in the prehospital environment, such as health evaluations, monitoring of chronic illnesses or conditions, and patient advocacy'?
questions.explanation: The deck defines community paramedicine as the model in which experienced paramedics get advanced training to provide added prehospital services such as health evaluations and chronic illness monitoring.
CARES is an external data registry, a core CQI tool that exposed a dispatch delay no one had measured.
questions.question: Atlanta's CARES registry linked 911, EMS, and hospital data and revealed that each 911 call passed through police and a county dispatcher before reaching EMS. After the process changed, the average time from 911 call to ambulance dispatch fell from 107 to 43 seconds. CARES served Atlanta EMS as what kind of tool?

questions.explanation: Selecting units and giving prearrival instructions are emergency medical dispatch functions.
questions.question: When a 911 call comes in, a trained dispatcher decides which units should respond and talks the caller through care until the crew arrives. What system is this?
Which term is defined as: federal legislation passed in 1996 whose main effect in EMS is limiting the availability of patients' health care information and penalizing violations of patient privacy?
choices: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)
questions.explanation: HIPAA, passed in 1996, limits access to patients' health care information and penalizes privacy violations.

questions.question: Trained personnel at a central call center receive a report of a house fire and coordinate the fire and EMS response. What facility are they working in?
questions.explanation: Managing incoming emergency requests is the job of the public safety access point.

questions.question: What is emergency medical dispatch (EMD)?
choices: A system that assists dispatchers in selecting appropriate units to respond to a call and provides callers with vital instructions until EMS crews arrive
A multidisciplinary system of professionals and agencies providing prehospital emergency care
Advanced life-saving procedures provided in the field
A provider trained in specific aspects of advanced life support
questions.explanation: Per the deck, EMD assists dispatchers in selecting appropriate units and provides callers with vital instructions until the arrival of EMS crews.

questions.question: What does the Americans With Disabilities Act do?
choices: It outlines the skills performed by various EMS providers
It protects people with disabilities against discrimination
It prevents injuries and illnesses from ever occurring
It gives the medical director oversight of care on each call
questions.explanation: The ADA is comprehensive legislation designed to protect people with disabilities against discrimination.

choices: The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA)
questions.explanation: HIPAA is the federal law that penalizes improper disclosure of patient information.
questions.question: A new EMT is told that sharing a patient's condition with a neighbor who is just curious could result in legal penalties for a privacy violation. Which law sets those penalties?

Los Medanos College in California could not prove that required skills testing had occurred for its 2019-2023 EMT classes, and about 247 graduates learned they had never been eligible for their certificates. What principle does this illustrate?
choices: Skills testing only matters for paramedic programs
Graduates are responsible for scheduling their own state audits
A program's certificate protects graduates even without records
If a program cannot prove testing happened, the state treats it as not done
questions.explanation: The deck states that if a program can't prove testing happened, the state treats it as not done, so EMTs should keep their own records.

questions.question: Under OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens standard, employers must offer the hepatitis B vaccination series at no cost to emergency responders within 10 days of initial assignment, and a worker who declines must sign a written declination form. This requirement follows the EMT into what?
choices: Employment: hepatitis B protection is treated as part of starting work as an EMT
A state EMS office enforcement action
questions.explanation: Federal workplace law treats hepatitis B protection as part of starting work as an EMT, which is why proof of the series, a titer, or a signed declination follows the EMT into employment.
That added IV and medication role identifies the advanced EMT.
questions.question: A crew member who has moved one step beyond basic EMT training is authorized to place an IV and administer a limited set of emergency drugs. What is this provider level called?

questions.explanation: EMTs provide basic life support, including use of an airway adjunct.
questions.question: At a collapse, a responder inserts an airway adjunct and begins basic life support care while the ambulance is readied for transport. Which provider level does this describe?

In Southfield, Michigan in 2020, a physician declared Timesha Beauchamp dead by phone based on a crew's report; she was later found breathing at a funeral home, and regulators found the paramedic had stopped CPR early and reported inaccurate vitals. What does this case show about online medical control?
choices: A termination-of-resuscitation order is only as reliable as the accurate, complete findings the crew reports to the physician
Physicians should never give orders by phone
Crews may stop CPR whenever they believe a patient is dead
Online medical control removes the crew's responsibility for patient assessment
questions.explanation: Ending resuscitation required a physician's order, and that order depended on an accurate crew report — the core of online medical control.
Emergency medical dispatch provides caller instructions while crews are en route.
questions.question: A caller is told step by step what to do for a choking child while the dispatcher sends the closest appropriate ambulance. Which dispatch function is being used?
Assessment in Action: What is the primary role of the EMT?
choices: Provide transport to the closest hospital
questions.explanation: Book's printed key: Ensure personal safety.

questions.question: YOU are the Provider (48-year-old woman, back pain): How is patient care integrated across health systems when a patient is transported to the hospital?
choices: By transferring medical control to the hospital at the moment the ambulance leaves the scene, ending the crew's documentation duties

Through communication with the receiving facility, starting with prenotification before arrival when appropriate, then a verbal report to receiving staff, followed by a more complete, detailed written report
Through the CQI process, which forwards the crew's run report to the hospital for review after the call
By credentialing, in which the receiving hospital verifies the crew's qualifications before accepting the patient
questions.explanation: Integrated care means communicating scene and history information to receiving staff, beginning with prenotification before arrival, then a verbal report followed by a detailed written report.

questions.question: In Colorado, two medical services companies hired a man whose paramedic certificate had expired in 2012 after accepting his forged documents; he treated over 100 patients. Where did credentialing fail?
choices: The state registry refused to share his records
The employers trusted applicant documents instead of checking the state registry
The man held a valid credential from another state
Credentialing was completed, but supervision was lacking
questions.explanation: The deck's connection: employer credentialing failed by trusting applicant documents instead of checking the state registry.

questions.question: In Aurora, Colorado, in 2019, paramedics injected Elijah McClain with 500 mg of ketamine, a dose for a roughly 200-lb man, though he weighed about 143 lb; he went into cardiac arrest and died. What lesson does this case teach about paramedic pharmacology?
choices: Sedative doses do not depend on patient weight
Ketamine should be given before any weight estimate is made
Weight-based dosing needs a careful estimate, and patients need monitoring after sedation
Only physicians may decide sedative doses in the field
questions.explanation: The deck's lessons are that weight-based dosing needs a careful estimate and patients need monitoring after sedation.

questions.question: Assessment in Action: This act of legislation protects people with disabilities from being denied access to programs and services that are provided by state or local governments.
questions.explanation: Book's printed key: Americans with Disabilities Act.

questions.question: What is a medical director in EMS?
choices: A system of reviews and audits aimed at improving outcomes
A device that detects shockable cardiac rhythms
The physician who authorizes or delegates to the EMT the authority to provide medical care in the field
Physician instructions given by radio or protocol
questions.explanation: The medical director is the physician whose authorization lets EMTs provide medical care in the field.

questions.question: What does the term "Knowledge-based failure" mean?
choices: Ongoing education that maintains, updates, and expands the EMT's knowledge and skills, and that each individual EMT is responsible for obtaining to keep certification.
An error that happens because the provider did not know the pertinent information — for example, giving the wrong drug because she did not know the information about that drug.
The criteria a person must meet to become licensed and employed as an EMT, which include proof of immunization against certain communicable diseases.
The state-level office that typically regulates the standards for prehospital emergency care and the individuals who provide it.
questions.explanation: Knowledge-based failure: An error that happens because the provider did not know the pertinent information — for example, giving the wrong drug because she did not know the information about that drug.
IV therapy and certain emergency medications are within the advanced EMT scope, which sits above the EMT but below the paramedic.
questions.question: On scene, a provider starts an IV line and gives a patient one of the emergency medicines her training and protocols allow, but she does not perform paramedic-level skills. What level of provider is she?
Assessment in Action: An example of teamwork and diplomacy is:
choices: using your persona to project a sense of personal superiority to patients.
being able to communicate while giving respect to the listener.
acknowledging that others are not in high regard or importance.
delegating multiple tasks only occasionally to ensure efficiency and safety.
questions.explanation: Book's printed key: being able to communicate while giving respect to the listener.

The trip record was completely accurate
The patient survived because of the crew's care
The agency had no effective quality assurance program
questions.explanation: The state found widespread problems, including no effective QA program, which let poor care and false documentation go uncaught.
questions.question: In Worcester, Massachusetts in 2008, paramedics walked a severe chest-pain patient down three flights of stairs against state protocol, and their trip record falsely claimed a stair chair was used; the patient died at the hospital. What did the state find about the agency's oversight?

In February 2023, the medical director of the Town of Eagle Point, Wisconsin EMS service resigned after complaining that providers were not following protocol; because state law requires a licensed medical director, the town had to suspend its EMS service until a new one was found. What does this case demonstrate?
choices: Medical directors are optional for small services
Without a medical director there is no legal authority to practice, so protocol compliance protects the service itself
A service can keep running indefinitely on standing orders alone
Protocol disputes have no effect on patient care
questions.explanation: No medical director means no legal authority to practice; Eagle Point's protocol dispute became a service outage.
He acted on knowledge he did not have, which is the definition of a knowledge-based failure.
questions.question: A provider picks a medication dose from memory, gets it wrong, and review shows he never learned the correct dose range. What kind of failure is this?

Freedom House Ambulance Service began in Pittsburgh in 1967 and trained unemployed Hill District residents, starting with 20 men, as some of the first US paramedics, working with Dr. Peter Safar; its standards became a national training model. What does this case show about the origin of the paramedic role?
choices: The role began in rural fire departments without any training
The profession began with community members who received rigorous training
Paramedics were originally hospital nurses reassigned to ambulances
The role was created by a federal law in 1967
questions.explanation: The deck's lesson is that the paramedic profession began with community members who received rigorous training.
An order given directly by radio or phone during the call is on-line medical direction.
questions.question: During a call, an EMT radios the hospital and a physician orders a medication dose in real time. What type of medical direction is this?

Which term is defined as: The 1966 National Academy of Sciences / National Research Council white paper that exposed how inadequate prehospital emergency care was; EMS as we know it today originated with its publication in 1966.

choices: A provider deliberately skips a required protocol step
A provider's gloved hand slips while starting an IV
A provider gives a drug without knowing its concentration
A provider's radio fails during a patient report

questions.question: Which of these errors is a knowledge-based failure?
Pickens County, Alabama lost its ambulance subsidy in 2024 and fell to a single ambulance before service ended entirely. What lesson does this case teach about primary service areas?
choices: Rural counties are exempt from designating a service area
Helicopters can permanently replace ground ambulances in a service area
A primary service area only works if someone can staff it and pay for it
A service area ends automatically when a subsidy expires
questions.explanation: The deck's connection: a primary service area only works if someone can staff it and pay for it.

questions.question: What does the term 'evidence-based medicine' mean?
choices: Efforts to limit the effects of an injury or illness that you cannot completely prevent
A call center staffed by trained personnel who manage requests for police, fire, and ambulance services
A health care model in which experienced paramedics provide additional services in the prehospital environment
An approach to medicine where decisions are based on well-conducted research, classifying recommendations based on the strength of the scientific evidence
questions.explanation: Evidence-based medicine bases decisions on well-conducted research, grading recommendations by the strength of the scientific evidence.

questions.question: What does the term "advanced life support" (ALS) mean?
choices: A multidisciplinary system of professionals and agencies providing prehospital care
Advanced life-saving procedures, some of which are now being provided by the EMT
Training in basic life support, including AED use and airway adjuncts
A dispatch system that provides callers with instructions until crews arrive
questions.explanation: Per the deck, advanced life support means advanced life-saving procedures, some of which are now provided by the EMT.
The team brought health care into the community rather than requiring a facility visit, which is the mobile integrated health care model.
questions.question: An EMS agency sends a team to a rural patient's home for a scheduled health check because the nearest clinic is an hour away. Which care model are they using?
What is an advanced EMT (AEMT)?
choices: A provider trained in basic life support, including AED use and assisting patients with certain medications
A system that helps dispatchers select units and gives callers instructions until crews arrive
A provider trained in specific aspects of advanced life support, such as intravenous therapy and giving certain emergency medications
The combined efforts of several professionals and agencies providing prehospital emergency care
questions.explanation: Per the deck, the AEMT is trained in specific aspects of advanced life support, including intravenous therapy and administration of certain emergency medications.

questions.question: Assessment in Action: Why is EMS research a vital part in the evolution of patient management?
choices: Research provides data that identify treatments that are beneficial and/or lifesaving for trauma patients and those that are not, and participation in research empowers the EMT to help shape the future of trauma care
Research is a continuing education requirement an EMT must complete to keep certification current
Research replaces CQI audits as the main way EMS systems check the quality of patient care
Research determines each state's scope of practice and the education standards for every provider level
questions.explanation: Book's printed key: Research provides data that identify treatments that are beneficial and/or lifesaving for trauma patients and those that are not. Participation in EMS research empowers the EMT to help shape the future of trauma care.

questions.question: Which term is defined as: "Efforts to prevent an injury or illness from ever occurring"?
choices: National EMS Scope of Practice Model
questions.explanation: The deck defines primary prevention as efforts to prevent an injury or illness from ever occurring.

National EMS Scope of Practice Model

choices: A federal law that sets one binding scope for every state
Oversight by the medical director to ensure care standards are met on each call
Efforts to prevent an injury or illness from ever occurring
A document created by NHTSA that outlines the skills performed by various EMS providers

In 2011, the Western Eagle County Ambulance District in rural Colorado launched one of the first community paramedic programs. Two paramedics made doctor-referred home visits — checking vitals, ECGs, blood draws, medications, and wounds — and wrote reports for the referring physicians. What does this program show about the community paramedic role?
choices: Community paramedics report home findings to the patient's referring physician, and hazards or missed medications found on a house call can prevent the next 911 run
Community paramedics replace primary care physicians for rural patients
Community paramedic visits are unplanned 911 responses rather than scheduled referrals
Community paramedics work without any physician involvement
